carried.name: Evening Listing, Relit
carried.summary: Round 11: #1 by score (mean 8.04, in 8 judges' top fours); carried as the best score of the round (clearly different here means 5.67 or more apart; the round's median is 9.45). Family: programme listing. Born in round 11 (informed). Evening Listing with the tube switched back on where the machine is live, lines drawn only where there is an order, and a head column that always says how things stand. This is Evening Listing's programme guide kept whole: slate bands with a head column, one-line rows read along a leader to tabular facts, and steel reverse video for "here". What comes back is the original tube's light, and only on a short list of what is live: the mark, "mind", Send, the box, the Now lamp, the status lamps, the monitors and her screen. Everything the family keeps stays matte. Lines appear only where there is an order, and every head column now says how its band stands. The feel is an evening TV listing lit by one real green tube: calm and easy to scan, with light exactly where the eye should go.

carried.name: Long Persistence
carried.summary: Round 11: #2 by score (mean 7.88, in 7 judges' top fours); carried as new family, not a near-duplicate: long-persistence instrument; nearest carried Evening Listing, Relit at 7.83. Family: long-persistence instrument. Born in round 11 (informed). The phosphor draws, the page prints: each page has one lit instrument that traces the family's own weeks, due dates or places with full bloom and afterglow, and every row of the graphite legend under it lights its mark. The light is the data. Each page with something in time or space gets one 4:3 P1 tube in a thin graphite case, and the tube draws that page's own data with the original's full effect: bloom, a 0.35px blur, scanlines, sheen, falloff, an 80px spill, a sweep beam with a wake of afterglow, and glowing marks that flare as the beam passes and never go out. Everything else is print: legend tables on graphite in bone ink with no glow. Pointing at a row lights its mark on the tube in 0.12s, and it fades over 1.2s. The page feels calmer and more grounded, and the green-screen tube is back, now doing a job: light only where attention belongs.

carried.name: Track Diagram Relit
carried.summary: Round 11: #3 by score (mean 7.52, in 4 judges' top fours); carried as new family, not a near-duplicate: mimic-line track; nearest carried Long Persistence at 7.01. Family: mimic-line track. Born in round 11 (phosphor mutant). Track Diagram with the tube switched back on: the same steel lines on slate boards, and everything the diagram marks as live (the now lamp, the status lamps, her screens, the monitors, the ring where it is your turn) glowing and breathing like phosphor again. This is Track Diagram with its tube switched back on. The signal box's diagram is kept whole: steel lines on green-black slate boards, a lamp at every stop, and times in a timetable margin. Everything it marks as the machine's, or as live, gives off light again the way the original green screen did. The monitors bloom and spill onto the page, her screens glow and pool light into her bubbles, and live lamps are white-hot points in a breathing phosphor halo. One rule carries the light through every page: the lamp where you are now is lit, and the section of track it stands on is lit from it, fading toward the next stop. The slate, the steel and the family's plates stay matte, so the page is calm and the light falls only where something is live.

carried.name: Signal Legend Relit
carried.summary: Round 11: #7 by score (mean 6.91, in 0 judges' top fours); carried as new family, not a near-duplicate: ruled composing room; nearest carried Track Diagram Relit at 6.16. Family: ruled composing room. Round 10: #3 by score (mean 7.48, in 4 judges' top fours); carried as new family, not a near-duplicate: ruled composing room; nearest carried Track Diagram at 6.15. Family: ruled composing room. Born in round 10 (phosphor mutant). Signal Legend with the tube switched back on: a layered halo on the mark, the key word, Send and every lit state, the monitors at full bloom with their green spill, and light that comes on at once and fades over a second. Signal Legend's system is kept whole: slate trays with their heads set into the rails, steel reverse video for "this one", square family surfaces and round machine glass. Its phosphor now gives off light the way a green-screen tube did, as a tight bloom inside a wide faint halo. It lights at once and fades over 1.2s. The lamp legend now reaches every page: #6dff9c means now or live, and each lamp is named. So Plans, Status, Home and the Settings card each have one glowing dot or small lit screen where their "now" is, and the rest of the page stays grounded, solid and quiet.

wildCarried.name: Flight Console
wildCarried.summary: Round 11: #12 by score (mean 6.67, in 1 judges' top fours); carried as the wild lane, for the ideas the judges most want developed (7 promise votes, #12 by score, today 4.71): violet flight console. Family: violet flight console. Born in round 11 (wild). The family's week run from a 1969 flight console: a violet flight-plan drawing leads every section, rows of lamps say how things stand, and the phosphor lights only what is live. Every page is a console in a 1969 mission control room, built from three materials that each have one job. Grey console bays carry engraved condensed legends. Violet flight-plan drawings on a faint plotting grid lead every section: a full drawing where the picture shows something the words do not, and a 76px pictogram tile everywhere else. #6dff9c appears only as light: the tubes, a lit lamp, the lit key word, the primary key, focus. The page should feel calm and exact. You read how things stand from rows of lamps and small readouts before you read a word, and the green monitors glow the way the original page's did.

wildCarried.name: Videotex Sommaire
wildCarried.summary: Round 11: #14 by score (mean 5.98, in 1 judges' top fours); carried as the wild lane, for the ideas the judges most want developed (5 promise votes, #14 by score, today 4.71): videotex service. Family: videotex service. Born in round 11 (wild). The family's own videotex service: one thing at a time under a mosaic band, numbered contents, a row of keys along the foot of every screen, and the phosphor lit on its terminal. FamilyDB is set out as a 1980s videotex service like the Minitel. Every screen opens with a band holding the page's mosaic picture, its name in double-height VT323 and its page-number tile, then shows one large thing, with a row of brown-plastic keys along the foot. Home is the terminal itself: a green tube fills the first screen above the keys, with Next up and a large radar at the top and the question and a blinking cursor at the foot of the glass, and a numbered Contents list sits beside it. The feel is a warm, calm public-service terminal where only the machine gives off green light.
